note: UTE G1 per-family retirement ledger (revised 2026-11-20 after the external review). The four terms are the owner's predicate (RetireAllowed = OldBaseline AND NewPathVerified AND SemanticDifferencesResolved AND NegativeControlsPass). Three rules the gate enforces and this ledger cannot talk its way out of: (1) `unit.familyId` is resolved against dev/agent-workflow/ledgers/arc-a-family-census.json, so a row cannot shrink the retirement unit to the tools it happened to verify; (2) coverage is derived from the baseline TSV's `entry` column and the new path's `NEW-PATH-VECTOR <id>` lines, so a member with no vector is refused rather than absorbed; (3) every declared `oldPath.files` entry is checked for presence, and scripts/eb3-family-definitions.mjs turns required CI red (DEF_RETIREMENT_UNLICENSED) if one is deleted while the row is not allowed. `state` remains a mirror of the computed verdict. See docs/plans/memo/ute-g1-20261120/RETIREMENT.md.

oldBaseline.note: 16 (request -> effect) vectors captured on the legacy host 0.2.0-rc.2 @ 639ed01539: 10 read/write/edit vectors plus 6 read_image vectors, ALL on the PRODUCT route-C seam (mountMemberA5sfRealm + attachA5sfNativeToolModules). RE-BASELINED 2026-11-20 by the route-C repair (UTE-3): until the repair the product route could not reach read_image at all (GAP-FS-CONTRACT-1 / PD-5, mount.ts merged only tools/systemPrompt into a routed module's deferred children), so a seventh vector (FS-I0-route-c-gap) pinned that product fact and FS-I1..I6 ran under a disclosed 'post-gap-1' composition. The repair continues a routed module's OWN declared fs into its deferred children, so FS-I1..I6 were re-captured on the PRODUCT composition and came out BYTE-IDENTICAL; the 10 read/write/edit rows are byte-identical to the reviewed baseline. FS-I0-route-c-gap was DELETED (not re-pointed: FS-I1 already is the in-lane allow baseline) and its fail-closed shape is still pinned by the world-factory FSB-IMG-1b fixture (`withheld-fs-continuation`), not by this fixture. The read_image rows' digest is over the bytes the ATTACHMENT STORE received, not the path string. The non-lane image denials carry distinct machine-readable classes (`missing-path`, `image-modality-denied`, `cancelled`); no corpus row uses the unclassified bucket `other`. Fixture identity in golden/old-path.meta.txt. This is the OldBaseline term for the FS family only — it says nothing about any other family.

newPathVerified.note: Prototype provider + the pinned next host's own ToolsService.execute; the 10 read/write/edit vectors are green on rc.5 (the 6 read_image baselines are newPathPending: the prototype has no image support until UTE-3 PR B2, so the gate correctly refuses UTE_VECTOR_UNREPRODUCED and does NOT cover read_image on this axis). This proves the PROTOTYPE path only: it is not a live boot, it does not prove read confinement (CLAIM_NOT_OBSERVABLE), and it must never be cited as a safety verdict.

differences.summary: old path FS_SANDBOX_DENIED vs new path FS_PERMISSION_DENIED (rc.5 tool-fs sandbox.ts:139-143 dereferences policy.mode). OWNER RULING 2026-11-20: route B+C adopted as the technical compatibility route — B keeps the native structured FsError (FS_PERMISSION_DENIED for a lane denial, never FS_SANDBOX_DENIED without the fs-sandbox protocol); C judges old/new compatibility through the closed refusal-category mapping in tests/ute-g1-fs/lib/refusal-categories.mjs, not by literal code equality. This is NOT a SemanticDifferencesResolved verdict and NOT an approval: approval PENDING (owner signature required).

old path refuses in prose, new path in typed FsError codes. OWNER RULING 2026-11-20: route B+C adopted (technical route only) — the corpus/harness compares a CLOSED refusal-category vocabulary implemented by tests/ute-g1-fs/lib/refusal-categories.mjs, which refuses (REFUSAL_VOCABULARY_INCOMPLETE) any unmapped legacy value or FsError code instead of defaulting it. Code-level equality is not required and is not claimed. APPROVAL: PENDING (owner signature required) — the term stays FALSE and retirement stays refused until the owner signs a reference-bound record.

semanticDifferencesResolved.note: Both recorded differences are retirement-blocking=YES and neither has an approval record, so this term is FALSE today by construction, not by opinion. The 2026-11-20 owner ruling adopted the B+C technical route (native structured FsError + a closed NINE-category refusal mapping that covers all seven refusal classes the corpus records, including the four the B1 read_image baselines added) and this row cites the implementing file (tests/ute-g1-fs/lib/refusal-categories.mjs) and the protocol memo (docs/plans/memo/ute-g1-20261120/FS-ERROR-PROTOCOL.md). The ruling did NOT resolve the differences and did NOT approve them: approval is PENDING (owner signature required). After B1 the gate refuses for the same two differences AND for UTE_VECTOR_UNREPRODUCED (the read_image baselines exist but no new-path run reproduces them), so unit=3/4 and state stays NOT_RETIREABLE; nothing here licenses retirement.

negativeControlsPass.note: Four family-level controls (NC-1 lane bites, NC-2 harness bites on a mutated golden cell, NC-3 no legacy fallback, NC-4 the lane is load-bearing) PLUS one real control per retirement-unit member on the legacy path: NC-MEMBER read (widen only the read lane -> the refusal becomes a leak), NC-MEMBER write (widen only the write lane -> the file appears), NC-MEMBER edit (drop only the edit version guard -> a stale edit applies), NC-MEMBER read_image (widen only the image read lane -> an out-of-lane image read materialises a 70-byte attachment). Each NC-MEMBER is paired with NC-MEMBER-POSITIVE proving the unmodified run still reproduces its golden row, so no control is vacuous. A green FS control is not evidence for Web or PTY.

families.note: FS is the first family in the UTE G1 ordering and may retire before Web/PTY (owner ruling: per-family retirement is incremental). Its retirement unit is the WHOLE assembly (read+write+edit+read_image, one candidate, PLANE_FS_FAMILY_INCOMPLETE on a partial mount) and the members are DERIVED from dev/agent-workflow/ledgers/arc-a-family-census.json, not from this row. UTE-3 PR B1 closes the OLD-PATH half for all four members (17 baseline vectors, per-member controls). It may NOT retire: the 7 read_image baselines are not yet reproduced by the prototype (UTE_VECTOR_UNREPRODUCED, PR B2 scope), read_image therefore has no new-path coverage (UTE_MEMBER_UNCOVERED on newPathVerified), and both semantic differences are retirement-blocking with no bound approval.
